# Appendix B — Software and reproducibility {#sec-appx-b}

## The series pattern

The analysis is a `{targets}` pipeline [@targetsr] in R, with `{renv}`
pinning package versions and one function per target. Paper 6 has its own
pipeline script and its own store, `_targets_p6.R` and `_targets_p6`,
following papers 4 and 5, so nothing it does can invalidate or overwrite the
published work of papers 1 to 5. `tar_config_set()` is never called anywhere
in paper 6: the setup chunk passes `store =` to each `tar_load()`, leaving
the project-root `_targets.yaml` that papers 1 to 3 share untouched.

Upstream objects — the runner table, paper 3's fitting and test matrices,
paper 5's test data, fitted rung-3b arm, stored configuration and published
backtests — are read from the main and paper-5 stores **read-only**, with
their content hashes recorded in `p6_upstream_fingerprint`. An upstream
change therefore invalidates this paper's downstream work rather than leaving
it silently stale.

Every number in this document is read from a target at render time via
`tar_read()` or `tar_load()`. None is transcribed.

## The one refit

Paper 6 changes no model, but it needed one thing paper 5 did not store: the
encoder's scores on the training split. `p5_fit_final_gru()` returns the
scores of the matrix it is handed, and paper 5 handed it the test matrix.

That function is therefore called twice, with paper 5's own configuration,
epoch count and seed, once scoring each split. Training is fully determined
by the seed and the data, and the scored matrix is read only after the last
gradient step, so both calls train the identical network. The first call's
test scores are asserted **bit-identical** to paper 5's stored
`p5_test_fit_rung3b$scores` — the observed maximum absolute difference is
`r sprintf("%.0f", p6_rung3b_scores$max_abs_test_diff)` — and the function
stops rather than continuing if they are not. Nothing in paper 5's store is
written.

```{r}
#| label: tbl-backend
#| tbl-cap: "Fitting environment, captured at fit time from inside the fitting function."
tibble::as_tibble(p6_rung3b_scores$backend) |>
  dplyr::transmute(
    torch = torch_version, libtorch = libtorch_version,
    R = r_version, Platform = platform,
    Device = device, `CUDA available` = cuda_is_available
  ) |>
  kable(align = "llllll")
```

The backend is the CPU build in double precision, the frozen parameter of
paper 5. Results do not reproduce across backends, so reproducing this
environment needs `CUDA = "cpu"` set before `{torch}` [@torchr] installs its
runtime; the lockfile pins R packages, not the C++ runtime underneath them.

## Gates

Three standing checks run on the pipeline graph, not as afterthoughts:

`scripts/verify_p6_ledger.R` — six assertions on the ledger. Three that it
rebuilds paper 5's published test backtest exactly under S1/K0, both against
the stored targets and against the printed figures; one that the corrected
each-way payout reproduces paper 2b's when given paper 2b's terms; one that
the corrected terms move exactly the rows the field-size ladder marks; one
that a staking rule changes stakes and not the bet set. Also on the graph as
`p6_ledger_gate`.

`p6_search_set_check` — row identity of the search set as a sorted set on
race and runner against paper 5's training frame, and zero overlap with test
race identifiers.

`p6_contrast_check` — paper 5's rung-1 rule, that a compared pair differs in
exactly one term, asserted over every contrast the paper reads before
anything is scored.

`p6_declaration_frozen` re-reads `DECLARED_RULES.md` from disk on every build
and matches it against the declaration target, so the committed artefact and
the pipeline cannot drift apart. `p6_declaration_check` fails the build if any
declared rule places fewer than 200 bets on the training split.

## Order of operations

The declaration was committed before any test target existed. The git history
records it: the commit introducing `DECLARED_RULES.md` contains no stage-2
target, and the stage-2 targets were added in the following commit. That is
the only mechanism available for a claim of this kind — a pre-registration
that lives in the same repository as the analysis is only as good as the
history that timestamps it.

## Running it

```
"C:/Program Files/R/R-4.6.0/bin/Rscript.exe" scripts/run_p6_pipeline.R
```

from the project root, via PowerShell — `{torch}` and the database connection
both fail under the Git Bash environment on the development machine. An
optional argument names a target to build up to, which is how the declaration
was frozen before the test targets were written.
